Share the treasure

The dragons want an equal share of their imaginary stones. Try these untimed puzzles aloud, on paper, or with small counters. Draw one circle for each dragon, then give each circle one mark at a time until you can’t make another full round.

The historical inventory credits Dragons Math Club to @prabathsilva (page 16). The puzzles are prototype interpretations. The first three also appear at Magic School; this page does not change the school lesson or record progress.

1. Three dragons

Share 12 stones among 3 dragons. How many stones does each dragon get?

Check puzzle 1

4 stones each. Three groups of 4 make 12, so none are left over.

2. Five dragons

Share 15 stones among 5 dragons. How many does each dragon get?

Check puzzle 2

3 stones each. Five groups of 3 make 15, so none are left over.

3. A bigger pile

Share 18 stones among 3 dragons. How many does each dragon get?

Check puzzle 3

6 stones each. Three groups of 6 make 18, so none are left over.

Bonus: stones left over

Share 14 stones among 4 dragons. Give each dragon as many whole stones as you can while keeping their shares equal. How many stones are left over?

Check the bonus

3 stones each, with 2 left over. A fourth full round would use 16 stones, so there aren't enough for one more each.
